notes: LIBRARY for the browser tools (no tools are registered here). snapshot.ts builds the accessibility-style page outline with short element refs that the agent clicks and types by; it reads Chrome's accessibility tree and DOM over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, which this app's engine (Servo) does not offer. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs: the only page access available is the `Browser` trait (evaluate JavaScript and get JSON back, input events, viewport, screenshot). So: port everything that is pure as is (outline formatting, ref assignment and bookkeeping, diffing, truncation, layout.ts in full with its test file, frame tree types and helpers), and replace the CDP data gathering with one JavaScript function evaluated in the page that walks the DOM and returns, as JSON, the same information the TypeScript took from the accessibility tree: role (computed from tag and ARIA attributes), accessible name, value, states, the element's box in CSS pixels, and a stable way to find the element again (store the element in a page-side map keyed by ref so later actions can reach it). Keep the output text format identical to the TypeScript for the same page structure. Public API: take a snapshot through `&dyn Browser`, resolve a ref to a point to click (center of its box, scrolled into view first), and run a small action on a ref through evaluate (focus, set value, read text). Same-origin iframes are walked in the same script; cross-origin frames are listed but not entered, and that limit is stated in the outline the same way the TypeScript marks frames it cannot read. Tests: unit tests for the pure parts (port layout.test.ts completely); for the page-side script, test the Rust side with a fake `Browser` that returns recorded JSON, and check the script itself for syntax by running it with bun or node against a tiny DOM stub if practical.
